findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous and ignores the folder-tree state
findings.body: The denial key is built as `name + "_" + parent` (cache.go:30-32) with no separator guarantee, so name `a_b` with parent `c` and name `a` with parent `b_c` give the same key. Kubernetes names rarely contain `_`, but the key can still collide. Also, a denial is stored for shortCacheTTL (30s, line 32). A grant made during that window is ignored, because the denial check runs before the permission cache and the DB. Before this change a denial was never cached on its own. Check that this staleness is acceptable. Consider a separator that cannot occur in names, such as a NUL byte or a length prefix.

findings.title: Cache-miss metric also counts identity lookup errors and cached-but-denied results
findings.body: `permissionCacheUsage("false")` is incremented whenever the cached path does not return Allowed. That includes a cache hit where the permission was not in the cached map, a render-service request (always uncached), and a GetUserIdentifiers error. The metric therefore mixes real misses with these cases. Previously it only counted a miss on permCache.Get.

contracts.action: Check consults a denial cache and the permission cache before the DB; List uses the permission cache first
contracts.equivalent_path: getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions previously read permCache internally; that read was moved up into getCachedIdentityPermissions
contracts.before_after: Before, the cache lookup was inside getUserPermissions. Now the callers look up the cache first and fall back to the DB. A cached allow returns early. A cached non-allow falls through to the DB. A denial found in the DB is stored in permDenialCache for 30s.
contracts.visible_effect: Fewer DB reads for repeated checks. A new grant can take up to 30s to take effect after a cached denial.
contracts.failure_mode: If the cached lookup errors, the code falls back to the DB path. The error is not logged or surfaced.

summary: The cache logic is correct. I found two minor issues: the denial key can collide, and a cached denial can hide a new grant for up to 30s. The cache-miss metric is also broader than a true miss.
